message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.55,"fairness_assessment":"A ranked, transparent vote fairly compares the three options, but fairness requires publishing lifecycle costs and assessing which user groups benefit or are excluded.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Favors dedicating the subsidy to expanding the children's book collection, prioritizing young readers and a clear, low-maintenance investment.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Favors creating an open-access digital space with computers, emphasizing broader access and digital inclusion while facing recurring-cost concerns.","influence":0.4},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Favors splitting the subsidy equally between books and digital access to balance constituencies, though this may underfund both projects.","influence":0.27}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"Use social-choice voting with ranked preferences and explicit feasibility criteria, followed by negotiation around a costed implementation plan. Agent B has a modest debate advantage, but the competing concerns about exclusion, recurring maintenance, and underfunding make a conditional compromise preferable to adopting any option without safeguards."}
